content: Women who are using combined injectable contraceptives (CICs), combined contraceptive patches and rings, progestogen-only pills (POPs), norethisterone enanthate (NET-EN), and levonorgestrel (LNG) or etonogestrel (ETG) implants are classified under Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) Category 2. This means that the advantages of using these methods generally outweigh the theoretical or proven risks. Women taking efavirenz or nevirapine, which are non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), can use depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) without any restrictions, as this is classified under MEC Category 1, indicating no restrictions for use. Women taking any NNRTI can generally use the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine device (LNG-IUD) if their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). This is classified under MEC Category 2, meaning the method is generally safe to use. However, women living with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) and taking any NNRTI should generally not initiate the use of the LNG-IUD until their illness has improved to an asymptomatic or mild stage. This is classified under MEC Category 3 for initiation, indicating that the risks usually outweigh the benefits in this scenario. For women taking any NNRTI who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and subsequently develop severe or advanced HIV clinical disease, there is no need to remove the IUD. This is classified under MEC Category 2 for continuation, meaning the method remains generally safe to continue using. Women using newer NNRTIs, such as etravirine and rilpivirine, can use all hormonal contraceptive methods without any restrictions. This is classified under MEC Category 1, indicating no restrictions for use. Women taking protease inhibitors (PIs) can generally use the LNG-IUD if their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). This is classified under MEC Category 2. Women living with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) and taking any PI should generally not initiate the use of the LNG-IUD until their illness has improved to an asymptomatic or mild stage. This is classified under MEC Category 3 for initiation. For women taking any PI who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and subsequently develop severe or advanced HIV clinical disease, there is no need to remove the IUD. This is classified under MEC Category 2 for continuation. Women using the integrase inhibitor raltegravir can use all hormonal contraceptive methods without any restrictions. This is classified under MEC Category 1. Women taking a rifampicin-based regimen (RI) can generally use the LNG-IUD if their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). This is classified under MEC Category 2. Women living with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) and taking an RI should generally not initiate the use of the LNG-IUD until their illness has improved to an asymptomatic or mild stage. This is classified under MEC Category 3 for initiation. For women taking an RI who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and subsequently develop severe or advanced HIV clinical disease, there is no need to remove the IUD. This is classified under MEC Category 2 for continuation. The Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) for contraceptive use provides evidence-based guidance on who can safely use various contraceptive methods. It is periodically updated to reflect new medical and scientific knowledge.
